key_insight: Prioritizing requests by cμ—holding-cost weight times effective service rate—is fluid-optimal for LLM inference scheduling under finite KV-cache memory.
engineering_relevance: Memory-aware priorities can reduce inference latency by accounting jointly for compute speed, memory bandwidth, and KV-cache capacity.
method: Model stochastic arrivals, heterogeneous request lengths, prefill, and decode under a finite KV-cache budget.
Reduce fluid dynamics to a multiclass single-server queue and prove cμ optimality.
Construct a feasible finite-system policy and prove convergence of its scaled dynamics to the optimal fluid policy.
evidence_signal: Experiments on a real LLM serving engine with an NVIDIA H800 report substantially lower average latency while maintaining high throughput; the abstract gives no numerical gains.
watch_item: Optimality is established in the fluid limit; finite-system benefits depend on practical implementation and workload characteristics.
paper_title: Asymptotic Optimality of $cμ$-Rule for LLM Inference Scheduling under Memory Constraint
